confirmations safe without a tty. Facts (all real, self-contained;
incident evidence: run-1786402322, 2026-08-10):
(1) THE INCIDENT: `spawner drain` was fired programmatically with both
confirmations piped (`printf 'y\ny\n' | spawner drain 0026 …`). The
parent process's stdin buffering consumed BOTH lines at the first
typer.confirm (the drain preview), so the spawned run's HITL breakpoint
read EOF, aborted, and the abort path destroyed finished work (see the
companion abort-path item). Programmatic firing is a legitimate
operator-attended pattern; today it fails late and destructively.

(a) EARLY REFUSAL: when stdin is not a tty and no explicit consent flag
is passed, `spawner drain` refuses at startup — before any preview
consumption or spawn — with a message naming the flag. A piped drain must
fail in the first second, not at the last gate.
(b) EXPLICIT CONSENT FLAG: add `--yes` to `spawner drain`, meaning:
auto-confirm the drain preview AND every forwarded spawn HITL for the
selected items. Print a loud one-line notice per auto-confirmed gate so
the transcript shows each gate was consumed by the flag. This is still
operator-fired and attended-by-authorization (ADR-0009's rung-2 posture);
it is NOT unattended scheduling — document that boundary in docs/drain.md.
(c) TTY PASSTHROUGH: when stdin IS a tty, behavior is unchanged
(interactive confirms).
(3) GUARDRAILS: unit tests for: non-tty without --yes refuses before
reading the queue's confirm (exit nonzero, clear message); --yes drains

tty path unchanged (prompt still issued). Update docs/drain.md (command
surface + the rung boundary note). Mark the ROADMAP finding ("Drain
confirmations require a tty…") Completed with a delivery note. Run the

import os
import sys
import typer

from kestrel_team.core.env import load_env

# Load .env once at the CLI boundary so every command (doctor/spawn/runs/resume)
# observes the same credential environment — doctor must not drift from spawn.
load_env()

app = typer.Typer(help="Kestrel orchestration control plane (the `spawner` CLI)")

from typing import Annotated, List


def prepare_workspace(repo: str, temp_dir: str) -> str:
    """Clone the target repo (local path or URL) into a disposable workspace.

    Clones into a `repo/` subdirectory of temp_dir (git clone needs an empty or
    absent target, and mkdtemp already created temp_dir) and returns that path.
    Only committed/tracked content is included -- untracked files, `.env`
    secrets, venvs, and caches in the source repo stay behind.
    """
    from kestrel_team.git.wrapper import GitWrapper

    workspace_path = os.path.join(temp_dir, "repo")
    GitWrapper.clone(repo, workspace_path)
    return workspace_path


def _workspace_has_unpushed_work(workspace_path: str) -> bool:
    """True when deleting `workspace_path` would destroy undelivered commits.

    The dogfood loss (run-1785159637): wrap-up aborted before pushing, then
    workspace cleanup deleted the only copy of the agent's completed commits.
    Cleanup must therefore refuse to delete any workspace whose branch has
    commits not yet on a remote.

    Conservative by design: a non-git directory (e.g. a failed clone) has
    nothing to preserve → False; a git workspace we cannot interrogate is
    preserved (→ True) rather than risk destroying work.
    """
    if not workspace_path or not os.path.isdir(os.path.join(workspace_path, ".git")):
        return False
    from kestrel_team.git.wrapper import GitWrapper
    try:
        return GitWrapper(workspace_path).unpushed_commit_count() > 0
    except Exception:
        return True

def resume(
    thread_id: str = typer.Argument(..., help="Thread id printed at run start (e.g. run-1751980000)"),
    force: bool = typer.Option(False, "--force", help="Resume even if the checkpointed workspace no longer exists on disk")
):
    """
    Resumes a previously checkpointed run from the persistent sqlite checkpoint store.
    """
    import os
    from kestrel_team.core.orchestrator import build_orchestrator
    from kestrel_team.core.persistence import get_checkpointer

    checkpointer = get_checkpointer()
    app_graph = build_orchestrator(checkpointer, interrupt_before=["wrap_up_node"])
    config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": thread_id}, "recursion_limit": 200}

    state_snapshot = app_graph.get_state(config)
    if state_snapshot is None or not state_snapshot.values:
        typer.echo(f"Error: No checkpoint found for thread '{thread_id}'.")
        raise typer.Exit(code=1)

    repo_path = state_snapshot.values.get("repo_path")
    if repo_path and not os.path.exists(repo_path):
        typer.echo(f"Warning: Checkpointed workspace '{repo_path}' no longer exists on disk. "
                   "Resuming will likely fail for any file operations.")
        if not force:
            typer.echo("Pass --force to resume anyway.")
            raise typer.Exit(code=1)

    run_config = state_snapshot.values.get("config") or {}
    if run_config.get("use_docker_sandbox") and not os.environ.get("KESTREL_SANDBOX_CONTAINER_ID"):
        typer.echo("Warning: This run was configured with use_docker_sandbox, but resumed runs do not "
                   "restart the sandbox container. Tools will run directly on the host.")

    typer.echo(f"Resuming thread: {thread_id}")
    if not (state_snapshot.next and "wrap_up_node" in state_snapshot.next):
        # Continue from the last checkpoint; this may run up to the HITL breakpoint.
        final_state = app_graph.invoke(None, config=config)
        state_snapshot = app_graph.get_state(config)

    if state_snapshot.next and "wrap_up_node" in state_snapshot.next:
        typer.echo("\n=== Human-in-the-Loop Breakpoint ===")
        typer.echo(f"The agent has completed the tasks. You can review the changes in the workspace: {repo_path}")
        confirm = typer.confirm("Proceed with Wrap-Up and Pull Request creation?")
        if not confirm:
            typer.echo("Aborted. Checkpoint and workspace left intact for a later resume.")
            raise typer.Exit(code=0)
        typer.echo("Resuming graph to create Pull Request...")
        final_state = app_graph.invoke(None, config=config)

    typer.echo("\n--- Agent Execution Complete ---")
    if final_state.get("messages"):
        typer.echo(final_state["messages"][-1].content)
    run_tokens = final_state.get("total_tokens", 0)
    run_cost = final_state.get("total_cost", 0.0)
    sub_estimate = final_state.get("subscription_cost_estimate", 0.0)
    max_budget = final_state.get("max_budget", 0.0)
    cost_report = f"Run Totals: {run_tokens} tokens | ${run_cost:.4f} cash"
    if sub_estimate:
        cost_report += f" | ${sub_estimate:.4f} subscription-usage estimate (not billed)"
    if max_budget:
        cost_report += f" (cash budget: ${max_budget:.2f})"
    typer.echo(cost_report)

@app.command()
def drain(
    ids: List[str] = typer.Argument(
        None, help="Queue item ids to drain (e.g. 0009); dash-boundary prefixes match"
    ),
    queue: str = typer.Option(
        None, "--queue", help="Queue directory (or set KESTREL_QUEUE_DIR)"
    ),
    group: str = typer.Option(None, "--group", help="Select items in this group slug"),
    risk: str = typer.Option(None, "--risk", help="Select items with this risk grade"),
    target: str = typer.Option(
        None, "--target", help="Select items whose target_repo contains this substring"
    ),
    limit: int = typer.Option(
        None, "--limit", "-l", help="Drain at most N selected items"
    ),
    list_only: bool = typer.Option(
        False, "--list", help="Print the preview table and exit without draining"
    ),
):
    """
    Deterministically drain shaped delegation items from the queue (ADR-0010).

    Selector-driven, never whole-queue by default: name items by id, or filter
    with --group / --risk / --target / --limit. `--list` previews and exits; a
    bare `spawner drain` previews the drainable items and asks for a selector; a
    selected drain previews then requires interactive confirmation before any
    spawn.
    """
    from kestrel_team.core import drain as drain_mod
    from kestrel_team.core.queue_items import (
        QueueDirError,
        QueueItemError,
        drainable_items,
        load_queue,
        resolve_queue_dir,
    )

    # Fail-closed queue resolution + load (design principle #1): a malformed item
    # halts the whole drain — it can never silently drop out of a batch.
    try:
        queue_dir = resolve_queue_dir(queue)
        items = load_queue(queue_dir)
    except (QueueDirError, QueueItemError) as e:
        typer.echo(f"Drain: {e}")
        raise typer.Exit(code=1)

    drainable = drainable_items(items)
    typer.echo(f"Queue: {queue_dir}")

    if not drainable:
        typer.echo("No drainable items in the queue (need mode: delegated + status: queued).")
        raise typer.Exit(code=0)

    has_selector = drain_mod.any_selector(ids, group, risk, target, limit)

    # `--list` and the bare invocation both PREVIEW and exit — they never spawn.
    # `--list` honours any filters given; a bare drain previews everything
    # drainable and asks for a selector (no selector ever implies "everything").
    if list_only or not has_selector:
        try:
            preview = drain_mod.select_items(
                drainable, ids=ids, group=group, risk=risk, target=target, limit=limit
            )
        except drain_mod.DrainSelectionError as e:
            typer.echo(f"Drain: {e}")
            raise typer.Exit(code=1)
        typer.echo(drain_mod.render_preview_table(preview))
        if not list_only:
            typer.echo(
                f"\n{len(preview)} drainable item(s). Pass a selector "
                "(item id, --group, --risk, --target, --limit) to drain, or "
                "--list to preview."
            )
        raise typer.Exit(code=0)

    # A selected drain: resolve the selection, preview it, and gate on an
    # interactive confirm before ANY spawn.
    try:
        selected = drain_mod.select_items(
            drainable, ids=ids, group=group, risk=risk, target=target, limit=limit
        )
    except drain_mod.DrainSelectionError as e:
        typer.echo(f"Drain: {e}")
        raise typer.Exit(code=1)

    if not selected:
        typer.echo("No drainable items match the selector.")
        raise typer.Exit(code=0)

    typer.echo(drain_mod.render_preview_table(selected))
    if not typer.confirm(f"\nDrain {len(selected)} item(s) now?"):
        typer.echo("Aborted. No items were drained.")
        raise typer.Exit(code=0)

    # Confirmed: the deterministic execution loop (mark running -> spawn ->
    # ledger match -> write back -> failure policy -> report). Attended: each
    # spawned run's own HITL breakpoint reaches the operator via inherited stdin.
    report = drain_mod.run_drain(selected, queue_dir=queue_dir)
    if report:
        typer.echo(report)

# `spawner drain` — the dispatcher lane (ADR-0010)

`spawner drain` is Kestrel's **thin deterministic drain** of shaped delegation
requests (ROADMAP V5, helm brief 0008 / ADR-0010). The queue lives in the intent
plane (kestrel-helm) as markdown items carrying intake-shaping frontmatter; this
repo reads those items **verbatim** and shells `spawner spawn` per selected item.
Loose coupling by design: files + CLI + ledger, never shared imports.

- The **item contract** (frontmatter fields, drainable rule, status lifecycle) is
  documented in [`queue_item_contract.md`](queue_item_contract.md).
- This document covers the **command surface**: how the operator selects items,
  previews them, and confirms a drain.

## Execution — the deterministic loop

After the operator confirms, `run_drain` executes the selection sequentially, in
queue order. Per item:

1. **Mark `running`** — the item file's `status:` is rewritten in place.
2. **Spawn** — `spawner spawn --team <team> --repo <target_repo> --goal <goal>`
   as a subprocess of this same CLI. Output streams through to the operator;
   stdin is inherited, so the run's own HITL breakpoint reaches the operator
   (the drain never answers it). For a `size_class: task` item the drain also
   passes **`--plan-cap 1`** (turn-economy, operator ruling 2026-08-07): the run
   caps its plan at a single step so a small item never pays multi-step planning
   overhead. This is judgment made **at intake** (ADR-0010) — the drain knows the
   item's `size_class` from the queue frontmatter and `spawn` does not, so it is
   the drain's job to pass the cap. No other size gets a cap. See
   [`queue_item_contract.md`](queue_item_contract.md) and the `--plan-cap` note
   below. Each spawn is a **fresh run** with its own thread id and checkpointed
   state, so its executor session starts **cold**: the warm-session layer
   (run-lifecycle §2) is warm only *within* one run's plan and is never resumed
   across drained items — that item boundary is an audit boundary, the same
   loose coupling this lane is built on.
3. **Match the ledger row** by the `Run thread: run-<epoch>` id scanned from the
   spawn output. The ledger is the drain's only source of run truth.
4. **Write back** — `delivered` when the row says `delivery: "delivered"`;
   `failed` otherwise (fail-closed: no row, or an `undelivered`/`skipped` run,
   is a failure — the drain never claims delivery the ledger doesn't show).
5. **Apply the item's pre-decided failure policy** (set at intake, ADR-0010):
   `low` → continue the batch; `medium` → halt remaining items sharing the
   failed item's group, continue independents; `high` → halt the whole batch.
   Halted items are untouched (still `queued`) and reported as skipped with the
   reason — a re-drain picks them up with the same selectors.

The drain ends with a report: one line per item (outcome, thread id, PR URL, the
ledger's cash vs subscription-estimate and governor vs executor token splits),
then a tally.

### Plan cap — `--plan-cap N` (task-class turn economy)

`spawner spawn` accepts an optional `--plan-cap N`. Today only the floor case,
**`--plan-cap 1`**, carries enforcement, and it is enforced **deterministically**
in the plan node (`kestrel_team/core/nodes/plan.py`): the run's plan is exactly one
step whose task is the goal text, and **LLM planning is bypassed entirely** — no
governor planning call is made, and no tokens are spent in the enforcement path.
The planner prompt is never trusted to self-comply; the cap is a hard code path,
not an instruction.

A value `N > 1` is currently **accepted but not enforced** — the plan node does
not truncate an LLM-generated plan to `N` steps, so only the `1` floor changes
behavior. The drain only ever passes `1` (below), so the dispatcher lane is exact;
the gap is on the attended `spawn` surface and is tracked as a proposed ROADMAP
finding.

The drain passes `--plan-cap 1` for `size_class: task` items and omits it for
every other size (which preserves the current multi-step LLM planning). The
motive is turn economy (operator ruling 2026-08-07): a task-class run that fans a
small item into several cold executor sessions burned 13.68M executor tokens
(run-1785766754) where a comparable single-session delivery cost 290k
(run-1785634142). On the subscription the cash is $0, but the wall-clock, quota,
and failure-at-the-cap costs multiply per step — so a `task`-size item is
collapsed to one step at the seam. `--plan-cap` is also available directly on
`spawner spawn` for an attended run.

## The queue

The drain reads `*.md` items (non-recursive) from a queue directory named by
`--queue <dir>` or the `KESTREL_QUEUE_DIR` environment variable. Resolution is
fail-closed: neither source set, or a directory that does not exist, is a
`QueueDirError` (the drain never invents a queue). A malformed item is a
`QueueItemError` that halts the whole command — a bad item can never silently
drop out of a batch. See the contract doc for the full field shape.

Only items with `mode: delegated` **and** `status: queued` are *drainable*; every
other item is read and validated but never selected.

## Selectors — never whole-queue by default

A drain that spawns runs **only what the operator's explicit selectors name**. No
selector ever implies "everything": a bare `spawner drain` previews and stops.
Selectors compose, applied in this order over the drainable items:

| Selector | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| positional ids (`spawner drain 0009 0010`) | Keep items whose id matches a token — the full filename stem or a dash-boundary prefix (`0009` matches `0009-lab-note`, but `000` does not). **Every token must match a drainable item, else a fail-closed `DrainSelectionError`** — a typo'd id never silently selects an empty batch. |
| `--group <slug>` | Keep items whose `group` equals the slug. |
| `--risk <grade>` | Keep items whose `risk_grade` equals the value. |
| `--target <substr>` | Keep items whose `target_repo` contains the substring (`--target scoop` matches `/repos/kestrel-scoop`). |
| `--limit N` | Keep at most the first `N` (the queue is id-sorted, so this is deterministic). `N` must be ≥ 1. |

Filters (`--group`/`--risk`/`--target`) that match nothing narrow to an empty
selection and the command reports "no items match" without spawning — they are
not identity claims, so an empty result is not an error. A positional id is an
identity claim, so a miss *is* an error. `--limit 1` on a low-risk item is the
smallest, earliest-acceptable drain (same blast radius as one attended run).

## Preview and confirmation

Every path that could spawn shows a preview table first —
`id · title · size · risk · failure policy · target`:

- **`--list`** prints the preview (honouring any selectors as filters) and
  **exits** without prompting or spawning.
- A **bare `spawner drain`** (no selector) prints the preview of all drainable
  items and exits, **asking for a selector**.
- A **selected drain** prints the preview of exactly the selected items, then
  requires an **interactive confirmation** (`typer.confirm`) before any spawn.
  Declining drains nothing.

```
$ spawner drain 0009
Queue: /path/to/queue
ID             TITLE                          SIZE   RISK  FAILURE  TARGET
-------------  -----------------------------  -----  ----  -------  --------------------
0009-lab-note  Lab note: governed delegation  small  low   low      /repos/kestrel-scoop

Drain 1 item(s) now? [y/N]:
```

## Non-judgment guarantee

The drain makes **no LLM calls**, adds **no retries** beyond what a single
`spawner spawn` already does, and **no selector ever implies "everything."** The
selection layer is pure filtering over validated items; the enforcement that a
real spawn carries (budget cutoff, retry cap, time-box, boundary audit, the
spawn HITL breakpoint, and the warm-session boundary — every drained run starts
its executor cold and cannot inherit another item's session) is unchanged —
attended drained runs still hit `spawn`'s own confirmation, which the drain
forwards to the operator. The `--plan-cap 1` the drain passes for `task` items
is not judgment either: it is a deterministic consequence of the item's
pre-decided `size_class` (set at intake), applied by a fixed rule, not an LLM
decision.

"""Selector + preview layer for `spawner drain` (helm brief 0008 / ADR-0010).

Part 2 of the drain MVP: turn the queue's validated ``QueueItem``s (parsed by
``queue_items``) into a *selected* subset via composable selectors, and render
the preview table the operator reads before any spawn.

Judgment-free by construction (the ADR-0010 non-judgment guarantee): selection is
pure filtering — no LLM calls, no retries, and **no selector ever implies
"everything"**. A drain that actually spawns runs only what the operator's
explicit selectors name; a bare invocation previews and stops. A positional item
id that names nothing is a fail-closed ``DrainSelectionError``, never a silent
empty batch — the same fail-closed stance the queue-item contract takes.

Import-light: stdlib + ``queue_items`` (+ the ledger reader at lookup time) — no
langchain/litellm, no run internals; the drain reaches the run machinery only
through the `spawner spawn` subprocess, the item files, and the runs ledger
(loose coupling per ADR-0010). ``run_drain`` is the deterministic execution
loop: mark running -> spawn -> match the ledger row by thread id -> write back
delivered/failed -> apply the item's pre-decided failure policy -> report.
"""
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from typing import List, Optional, Sequence

from kestrel_team.core.queue_items import QueueItem, set_item_status


class DrainSelectionError(Exception):
    """A selector is invalid or names no drainable item.

    Fail-closed: a typo'd item id or a non-positive ``--limit`` is a named error,
    so the operator learns their selector missed rather than watching an empty
    (or wrong) batch run. Filters that simply match nothing are not an error —
    they narrow to an empty selection the caller can report — but a positional id
    is an identity claim, so a miss is fatal.
    """


# The preview title column is capped so one long brief title cannot smear the
# whole table; the full title lives in the item file, not this operator preview.
_TITLE_MAX = 44

_PREVIEW_HEADERS = ("ID", "TITLE", "SIZE", "RISK", "FAILURE", "TARGET")


def any_selector(
    ids: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None,
    group: Optional[str] = None,
    risk: Optional[str] = None,
    target: Optional[str] = None,
    limit: Optional[int] = None,
) -> bool:
    """True if the operator supplied any selector at all.

    A bare ``spawner drain`` (every argument falsy/None) supplies none — it
    previews and stops rather than defaulting to the whole queue.
    """
    return bool(ids) or group is not None or risk is not None \
        or target is not None or limit is not None


def select_items(
    drainables: Sequence[QueueItem],
    *,
    ids: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None,
    group: Optional[str] = None,
    risk: Optional[str] = None,
    target: Optional[str] = None,
    limit: Optional[int] = None,
) -> List[QueueItem]:
    """Resolve composable selectors over the drainable items, in order.

    ``drainables`` must already be the drainable subset (delegated + queued);
    selection never reaches non-drainable items. The selectors compose:

    1. **positional ids** — keep items matching any given id token
       (``QueueItem.matches_id``: full stem or a dash-boundary prefix). Every
       token MUST match at least one drainable item, else ``DrainSelectionError``
       — a positional id is an identity claim, so a miss is fail-closed.
    2. **--group** — keep items whose ``group`` equals the slug.
    3. **--risk** — keep items whose ``risk_grade`` equals the value.
    4. **--target** — keep items whose ``target_repo`` contains the value as a
       substring (so ``--target scoop`` matches ``/repos/kestrel-scoop``).
    5. **--limit N** — keep at most the first ``N`` (deterministic: the queue is
       already id-sorted). ``N`` must be >= 1, else ``DrainSelectionError``.

    Result order follows the id-sorted queue; duplicates (an item matched by two
    id tokens, or by a prefix token) appear once.
    """
    if limit is not None and limit < 1:
        raise DrainSelectionError(
            f"--limit must be a positive integer, got {limit}."
        )

    selected: List[QueueItem] = list(drainables)

    if ids:
        selected_ids: set = set()
        for token in ids:
            matched = [item for item in drainables if item.matches_id(token)]
            if not matched:
                raise DrainSelectionError(
                    f"No drainable item matches id '{token}'. "
                    "Run `spawner drain --list` to see the drainable items."
                )
            selected_ids.update(item.item_id for item in matched)
        # Preserve the id-sorted order of `drainables`; dedupe via the id set.
        selected = [item for item in drainables if item.item_id in selected_ids]

    if group is not None:
        selected = [item for item in selected if item.group == group]
    if risk is not None:
        selected = [item for item in selected if item.risk_grade == risk]
    if target is not None:
        selected = [item for item in selected if target in item.target_repo]

    if limit is not None:
        selected = selected[:limit]

    return selected


def _truncate(text: str, width: int) -> str:
    text = text or ""
    if len(text) <= width:
        return text
    if width <= 1:
        return text[:width]
    return text[: width - 1] + "…"


def render_preview_table(items: Sequence[QueueItem]) -> str:
    """Render the operator preview: id, title, size, risk, failure policy,
    target — one row per item, columns aligned. Empty selection renders a
    single ``(no drainable items)`` line rather than a bare header."""
    if not items:
        return "(no drainable items)"

    rows = [
        (
            item.item_id,
            _truncate(item.title, _TITLE_MAX),
            item.size_class,
            item.risk_grade,
            item.failure_policy,
            item.target_repo,
        )
        for item in items
    ]

    widths = [len(h) for h in _PREVIEW_HEADERS]
    for row in rows:
        for i, cell in enumerate(row):
            widths[i] = max(widths[i], len(cell))

    def _fmt(cells: Sequence[str]) -> str:
        return "  ".join(cell.ljust(widths[i]) for i, cell in enumerate(cells))

    lines = [_fmt(_PREVIEW_HEADERS), _fmt(tuple("-" * w for w in widths))]
    lines.extend(_fmt(row) for row in rows)
    return "\n".join(lines)


# --- Execution (part 3): the deterministic loop -------------------------------
#
# Loose coupling per ADR-0010: the drain reaches the run machinery ONLY through
# the `spawner spawn` subprocess, the queue item files, and the runs ledger —
# never by importing run internals. Judgment-free: no LLM calls, no retries
# beyond what a single spawn already does; every decision below was made at
# intake (the item's pre-decided failure policy) or by the operator (the
# confirmed selection).

_THREAD_ID_RE = re.compile(r"Run thread: (run-\d+)")

# Ledger lookback for matching a just-finished run. The ledger appends one row
# per run, so the row we want is at the tail; 200 is far beyond any drain batch.
_LEDGER_LOOKBACK = 200


def _spawn_command(item: QueueItem) -> List[str]:
    """The exact `spawner spawn` argv for one queue item — same CLI, new process.

    Judgment at intake (ADR-0010): the drain knows each item's ``size_class`` from
    the queue frontmatter; ``spawn`` does not. A ``task``-size item never pays
    multi-step planning overhead (operator ruling 2026-08-07, turn-economy), so
    the drain passes ``--plan-cap 1`` for those items and nothing otherwise —
    spawn then caps the plan at one step (LLM planning bypassed in ``plan_node``).
    """
    cmd = [
        sys.executable,
        "-m",
        "kestrel_team.cli.app",
        "spawn",
        "--team",
        item.team,
        "--repo",
        item.target_repo,
        "--goal",
        item.read_goal(),
    ]
    if item.size_class == "task":
        cmd += ["--plan-cap", "1"]
    return cmd


def _invoke_spawn(item: QueueItem, *, forward_stdin: bool = True) -> tuple:
    """Run one item's spawn as a subprocess; return (returncode, thread_id).

    Stdout is streamed through to the operator line by line (an attended drain
    watches its runs) while being scanned for the ``Run thread: run-<epoch>``
    line — the only fact the drain needs from the output. Stdin is inherited by
    default so spawn's own HITL breakpoint reaches the operator; the drain never
    answers it (``forward_stdin=False`` closes stdin, so an unattended caller
    gets spawn's fail-safe abort path rather than a silent auto-confirm).
    """
    proc = subprocess.Popen(
        _spawn_command(item),
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
        stdin=None if forward_stdin else subprocess.DEVNULL,
        text=True,
    )
    thread_id = None
    for line in proc.stdout:
        print(line, end="")
        if thread_id is None:
            match = _THREAD_ID_RE.search(line)
            if match:
                thread_id = match.group(1)
    proc.wait()
    return proc.returncode, thread_id


def _ledger_row_for(thread_id: str):
    """The ledger row for ``thread_id``, or None. The ledger is the drain's only
    source of run truth (delivery state, PR URL, cost splits) — never the spawn's
    exit code alone."""
    from kestrel_team.core.ledger import read_runs

    for row in read_runs(limit=_LEDGER_LOOKBACK):
        if row.get("thread_id") == thread_id:
            return row
    return None


def run_drain(items: Sequence[QueueItem], *, queue_dir: str, forward_stdin: bool = True) -> str:
    """The deterministic execution loop (ADR-0010 §4), sequential MVP.

    Per selected item, in queue order: mark ``running`` in the item file, shell
    ``spawner spawn``, match the run's ledger row by thread id, write back
    ``delivered`` (ledger ``delivery == "delivered"``) or ``failed``, then apply
    the item's pre-decided failure policy:

      low    -> continue the batch;
      medium -> halt remaining items sharing the failed item's group,
                continue independents;
      high   -> halt the whole batch.

    Halted items are never touched — they stay ``queued`` and are reported as
    skipped with the reason, so a re-drain picks them up by the same selectors.
    An item whose run produced no ledger row is ``failed`` (fail-closed: no row,
    no delivery claim). Returns the drain report.
    """
    results = []  # (item, outcome, thread_id, row, note)
    halted_groups: set = set()
    halt_batch = False

    for item in items:
        if halt_batch:
            results.append(
                (item, "skipped", None, None, "batch halted by a high-policy failure")
            )
            continue
        if item.group and item.group in halted_groups:
            results.append(
                (
                    item,
                    "skipped",
                    None,
                    None,
                    f"group '{item.group}' halted by a medium-policy failure",
                )
            )
            continue

        set_item_status(item.path, "running")
        returncode, thread_id = _invoke_spawn(item, forward_stdin=forward_stdin)

        row = _ledger_row_for(thread_id) if thread_id else None
        if row is not None and row.get("delivery") == "delivered":
            set_item_status(item.path, "delivered")
            results.append((item, "delivered", thread_id, row, ""))
            continue

        set_item_status(item.path, "failed")
        if thread_id is None:
            note = f"spawn exited {returncode} before a run started"
        elif row is None:
            note = "no ledger row found for the run"
        else:
            note = f"run ended with delivery: {row.get('delivery')!r}"
        results.append((item, "failed", thread_id, row, note))

        if item.failure_policy == "high":
            halt_batch = True
        elif item.failure_policy == "medium" and item.group:
            halted_groups.add(item.group)
        # low -> continue the batch.

    return _render_report(results)


def _render_report(results: Sequence[tuple]) -> str:
    """The end-of-drain report: one line per item (outcome, thread id, PR, the
    ledger's cash/subscription and governor/executor splits), then a tally."""
    lines = ["", "=== Drain report ==="]
    tally: dict = {}
    for item, outcome, thread_id, row, note in results:
        tally[outcome] = tally.get(outcome, 0) + 1
        parts = [f"{item.item_id}: {outcome}"]
        if thread_id:
            parts.append(thread_id)
        if row:
            if row.get("pr_url"):
                parts.append(str(row["pr_url"]))
            cash = row.get("total_cost")
            estimate = row.get("subscription_cost_estimate")
            if cash is not None:
                parts.append(f"${cash:.4f} cash")
            if estimate:
                parts.append(f"${estimate:.4f} subscription-estimate")
            gov, execu = row.get("governor_tokens"), row.get("executor_tokens")
            if gov is not None and execu is not None:
                parts.append(f"tokens {gov} governor / {execu} executor")
        if note:
            parts.append(f"({note})")
        lines.append("  " + " | ".join(parts))
    summary = ", ".join(f"{count} {name}" for name, count in sorted(tally.items()))
    lines.append(f"Drained: {summary}.")
    return "\n".join(lines)

"""Non-tty consent gating for the CLI's confirmation prompts.

Every gate Kestrel puts in front of spend (the drain preview, the spawn HITL
breakpoint) is a `typer.confirm` read from stdin. Without a terminal those reads
are unsafe in a specific, demonstrated way (run-1786402322, 2026-08-10): a drain
fired programmatically with both answers piped
(``printf 'y\\ny\\n' | spawner drain 0026 …``) had BOTH lines consumed by the
parent's buffered read at the FIRST confirm, so the spawned run's HITL read EOF,
aborted, and the abort path destroyed finished work. The failure came last and
cost the whole run.

So consent is fail-closed and explicit — never inferred from bytes on a pipe:

* ``stdin_is_tty()`` — is a human actually behind stdin?
* ``refuse_without_tty()`` — when they are not and no consent flag was passed,
  refuse at STARTUP, before any gate is consumed or any run spawned.
* ``confirm_gate()`` — the single confirm seam: with ``assume_yes`` it prints a
  loud one-line notice naming the gate the flag consumed (so the transcript
  shows every gate that went unasked) and returns True; otherwise it prompts
  exactly as before, so the tty path is unchanged.

``--yes`` is *attended-by-authorization* (ADR-0009 rung 2): an operator fired the
command and pre-authorized its gates in the same breath. It is NOT rung-3
unattended scheduling — nothing here lets a timer spend money.

Import-light: stdlib + typer.
"""
import sys

import typer

# Loud by construction: an auto-confirmed gate must be greppable in a
# transcript, one line per gate, so an audit can count the gates the flag ate.
_NOTICE = "!! --yes AUTO-CONFIRMED: {gate} (no prompt was issued; consent came from the flag)"


def stdin_is_tty() -> bool:
    """True when stdin is an interactive terminal.

    Conservative: a detached, closed, or non-reporting stdin is NOT a tty, so
    the callers below refuse rather than prompt into the void.
    """
    stream = sys.stdin
    if stream is None:
        return False
    try:
        return bool(stream.isatty())
    except (AttributeError, ValueError):  # detached or closed stream
        return False


def refuse_without_tty(command: str, gates: str, flag: str = "--yes") -> None:
    """Refuse `command` when stdin cannot answer its gates and no flag consented.

    Raises ``typer.Exit(1)`` after printing the remedy (design principle: error
    messages carry remedies). Call this BEFORE the work that leads to a gate —
    a piped invocation must fail in the first second, not at the last prompt
    after a run has already been spawned and paid for.
    """
    typer.echo(
        f"{command} refused: stdin is not a terminal, so {gates} cannot be "
        f"answered interactively."
    )
    typer.echo(
        "Piped answers do NOT work: the first confirm's buffered read consumes "
        "every piped line, and the next gate then reads EOF and aborts "
        "(run-1786402322)."
    )
    typer.echo(
        f"Remedy: re-run attached to a terminal, or pass {flag} to auto-confirm "
        f"{gates} for the selected work. {flag} is operator-fired consent "
        "(attended-by-authorization, ADR-0009 rung 2) — it is not unattended "
        "scheduling."
    )
    raise typer.Exit(code=1)


def confirm_gate(prompt: str, *, gate: str, assume_yes: bool = False) -> bool:
    """The single confirm seam: prompt, or auto-confirm loudly under ``--yes``.

    ``gate`` names the gate in the auto-confirm notice (e.g. "the drain preview
    gate", "the spawn HITL breakpoint for run-…"). With ``assume_yes`` false the
    behavior is exactly ``typer.confirm`` — the interactive tty path is
    unchanged.
    """
    if assume_yes:
        typer.echo(_NOTICE.format(gate=gate))
        return True
    return typer.confirm(prompt)

import os

import pytest

from kestrel_team.core import drain as drain_mod
from kestrel_team.core.queue_items import QueueItem


def _item_text(**overrides):
    fields = {
        "size_class": "small",
        "risk_grade": "low",
        "failure_policy": "low",
        "mode": "delegated",
        "group": "lab-notes",
        "status": "queued",
        # A non-engine product repo: low risk is legitimate (the engine risk
        # floor only applies to the factory's own tool repos).
        "target_repo": "/repos/artemis-home",
        "team": "claude_squad",
        "goal": "Do the shaped thing.",
    }
    fields.update(overrides)
    lines = ["---"]
    for key, value in fields.items():
        if value is None:
            continue
        lines.append(f"{key}: {value}")
    lines.append("---")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append("# A title")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def _make_item(tmp_path, name, **overrides):
    path = os.path.join(str(tmp_path), name)
    with open(path, "w") as f:
        f.write(_item_text(**overrides))
    return QueueItem.from_file(path)


def _status_on_disk(item):
    return QueueItem.from_file(item.path).status


def _scripted(monkeypatch, outcomes, delivered_rows):
    """Script the loop's two seams.

    ``outcomes`` maps item_id -> (returncode, thread_id); ``delivered_rows`` maps
    thread_id -> ledger row (absent id -> no row). Records the statuses each item
    file held AT SPAWN TIME so tests can assert the running transition.
    """
    spawned = []
    statuses_at_spawn = {}

    def fake_invoke(item, forward_stdin=True):
        spawned.append(item.item_id)
        statuses_at_spawn[item.item_id] = _status_on_disk(item)
        return outcomes[item.item_id]

    def fake_row(thread_id):
        return delivered_rows.get(thread_id)

    monkeypatch.setattr(drain_mod, "_invoke_spawn", fake_invoke)
    monkeypatch.setattr(drain_mod, "_ledger_row_for", fake_row)
    return spawned, statuses_at_spawn


def _delivered_row(thread_id, **extra):
    row = {
        "thread_id": thread_id,
        "delivery": "delivered",
        "pr_url": f"https://github.com/x/y/pull/9",
        "total_cost": 0.0042,
        "subscription_cost_estimate": 1.5,
        "governor_tokens": 100,
        "executor_tokens": 900,

# `spawner drain` — the dispatcher lane (ADR-0010)

`spawner drain` is Kestrel's **thin deterministic drain** of shaped delegation
requests (ROADMAP V5, helm brief 0008 / ADR-0010). The queue lives in the intent
plane (kestrel-helm) as markdown items carrying intake-shaping frontmatter; this
repo reads those items **verbatim** and shells `spawner spawn` per selected item.
Loose coupling by design: files + CLI + ledger, never shared imports.

- The **item contract** (frontmatter fields, drainable rule, status lifecycle) is
  documented in [`queue_item_contract.md`](queue_item_contract.md).
- This document covers the **command surface**: how the operator selects items,
  previews them, and confirms a drain.

## Execution — the deterministic loop

After the operator confirms, `run_drain` executes the selection sequentially, in
queue order. Per item:

1. **Mark `running`** — the item file's `status:` is rewritten in place.
2. **Spawn** — `spawner spawn --team <team> --repo <target_repo> --goal <goal>`
   as a subprocess of this same CLI. Output streams through to the operator;
   stdin is inherited, so the run's own HITL breakpoint reaches the operator
   (the drain never answers it). For a `size_class: task` item the drain also
   passes **`--plan-cap 1`** (turn-economy, operator ruling 2026-08-07): the run
   caps its plan at a single step so a small item never pays multi-step planning
   overhead. This is judgment made **at intake** (ADR-0010) — the drain knows the
   item's `size_class` from the queue frontmatter and `spawn` does not, so it is
   the drain's job to pass the cap. No other size gets a cap. See
   [`queue_item_contract.md`](queue_item_contract.md) and the `--plan-cap` note
   below. Each spawn is a **fresh run** with its own thread id and checkpointed
   state, so its executor session starts **cold**: the warm-session layer
   (run-lifecycle §2) is warm only *within* one run's plan and is never resumed
   across drained items — that item boundary is an audit boundary, the same
   loose coupling this lane is built on.
3. **Match the ledger row** by the `Run thread: run-<epoch>` id scanned from the
   spawn output. The ledger is the drain's only source of run truth.
4. **Write back** — `delivered` when the row says `delivery: "delivered"`;
   `failed` otherwise (fail-closed: no row, or an `undelivered`/`skipped` run,
   is a failure — the drain never claims delivery the ledger doesn't show).
5. **Apply the item's pre-decided failure policy** (set at intake, ADR-0010):
   `low` → continue the batch; `medium` → halt remaining items sharing the
   failed item's group, continue independents; `high` → halt the whole batch.
   Halted items are untouched (still `queued`) and reported as skipped with the
   reason — a re-drain picks them up with the same selectors.

The drain ends with a report: one line per item (outcome, thread id, PR URL, the
ledger's cash vs subscription-estimate and governor vs executor token splits),
then a tally.

### Plan cap — `--plan-cap N` (task-class turn economy)

`spawner spawn` accepts an optional `--plan-cap N`. Today only the floor case,
**`--plan-cap 1`**, carries enforcement, and it is enforced **deterministically**
in the plan node (`kestrel_team/core/nodes/plan.py`): the run's plan is exactly one
step whose task is the goal text, and **LLM planning is bypassed entirely** — no
governor planning call is made, and no tokens are spent in the enforcement path.
The planner prompt is never trusted to self-comply; the cap is a hard code path,
not an instruction.

A value `N > 1` is currently **accepted but not enforced** — the plan node does
not truncate an LLM-generated plan to `N` steps, so only the `1` floor changes
behavior. The drain only ever passes `1` (below), so the dispatcher lane is exact;
the gap is on the attended `spawn` surface and is tracked as a proposed ROADMAP
finding.

The drain passes `--plan-cap 1` for `size_class: task` items and omits it for
every other size (which preserves the current multi-step LLM planning). The
motive is turn economy (operator ruling 2026-08-07): a task-class run that fans a
small item into several cold executor sessions burned 13.68M executor tokens
(run-1785766754) where a comparable single-session delivery cost 290k
(run-1785634142). On the subscription the cash is $0, but the wall-clock, quota,
and failure-at-the-cap costs multiply per step — so a `task`-size item is
collapsed to one step at the seam. `--plan-cap` is also available directly on
`spawner spawn` for an attended run.

## The queue

The drain reads `*.md` items (non-recursive) from a queue directory named by
`--queue <dir>` or the `KESTREL_QUEUE_DIR` environment variable. Resolution is
fail-closed: neither source set, or a directory that does not exist, is a
`QueueDirError` (the drain never invents a queue). A malformed item is a
`QueueItemError` that halts the whole command — a bad item can never silently
drop out of a batch. See the contract doc for the full field shape.

Only items with `mode: delegated` **and** `status: queued` are *drainable*; every
other item is read and validated but never selected.

## Selectors — never whole-queue by default

A drain that spawns runs **only what the operator's explicit selectors name**. No
selector ever implies "everything": a bare `spawner drain` previews and stops.
Selectors compose, applied in this order over the drainable items:

| Selector | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| positional ids (`spawner drain 0009 0010`) | Keep items whose id matches a token — the full filename stem or a dash-boundary prefix (`0009` matches `0009-lab-note`, but `000` does not). **Every token must match a drainable item, else a fail-closed `DrainSelectionError`** — a typo'd id never silently selects an empty batch. |
| `--group <slug>` | Keep items whose `group` equals the slug. |
| `--risk <grade>` | Keep items whose `risk_grade` equals the value. |
| `--target <substr>` | Keep items whose `target_repo` contains the substring (`--target scoop` matches `/repos/kestrel-scoop`). |
| `--limit N` | Keep at most the first `N` (the queue is id-sorted, so this is deterministic). `N` must be ≥ 1. |

Filters (`--group`/`--risk`/`--target`) that match nothing narrow to an empty
selection and the command reports "no items match" without spawning — they are
not identity claims, so an empty result is not an error. A positional id is an
identity claim, so a miss *is* an error. `--limit 1` on a low-risk item is the
smallest, earliest-acceptable drain (same blast radius as one attended run).

## Preview and confirmation

Every path that could spawn shows a preview table first —
`id · title · size · risk · failure policy · target`:

- **`--list`** prints the preview (honouring any selectors as filters) and
  **exits** without prompting or spawning.
- A **bare `spawner drain`** (no selector) prints the preview of all drainable
  items and exits, **asking for a selector**.
- A **selected drain** prints the preview of exactly the selected items, then
  requires an **interactive confirmation** (`typer.confirm`) before any spawn.
  Declining drains nothing.

```
$ spawner drain 0009
Queue: /path/to/queue
ID             TITLE                          SIZE   RISK  FAILURE  TARGET
-------------  -----------------------------  -----  ----  -------  --------------------
0009-lab-note  Lab note: governed delegation  small  low   low      /repos/kestrel-scoop

Drain 1 item(s) now? [y/N]:
```

## Non-judgment guarantee

The drain makes **no LLM calls**, adds **no retries** beyond what a single
`spawner spawn` already does, and **no selector ever implies "everything."** The
selection layer is pure filtering over validated items; the enforcement that a
real spawn carries (budget cutoff, retry cap, time-box, boundary audit, the
spawn HITL breakpoint, and the warm-session boundary — every drained run starts
its executor cold and cannot inherit another item's session) is unchanged —
attended drained runs still hit `spawn`'s own confirmation, which the drain
forwards to the operator. The `--plan-cap 1` the drain passes for `task` items
is not judgment either: it is a deterministic consequence of the item's
pre-decided `size_class` (set at intake), applied by a fixed rule, not an LLM
decision.

# Kestrel

A control plane for spawning, governing, and auditing time-boxed agent teams that deliver work as pull requests.

## What is this

Kestrel does not compete with frontier agent harnesses on the inner loop — it governs them. The differentiated layer is everything around execution: team manifests, time-boxed spawning, disposable clone workspaces, an optional Docker sandbox, permitted-path enforcement, budget cutoffs and token telemetry, Steering Gateway governance, and PR delivery with a human approval gate. A run is a bounded unit of agentic labor: you give it a goal, a repo, a time box, and a budget; it hands back a pull request and a ledger record.

Execution itself is a pluggable Executor chosen per persona: the built-in native LLM + tool loop (any provider via LiteLLM), or a headless frontier CLI agent — Claude Code (`claude -p`) running inside the sandbox.

## How it fits together

```
spawner CLI ──> disposable workspace (git clone + feat/agent-<ts> branch)
   │                       │ (optional) Docker sandbox mounts it at /workspace
   └─> LangGraph loop: plan ─> supervise ─> execute ─> review ─┐
             ▲   (native LLM loop  or  Claude Code CLI)        │ approve/next task
             └────────────── reject: retry with feedback ──────┘
   done / time-box / retry-cap / budget ─> wrap-up: commit, PR (after human confirm)
   every run ─> ledger record in ~/.kestrel/runs.jsonl
```

## Install

Requires Python >= 3.10 (plus `git`, and the `gh` CLI for PR creation).

```bash
python -m venv venv
venv/bin/pip install .
venv/bin/pip install pytest   # to run the test suite
```

Honest note: `pyproject.toml` is Poetry-format but `poetry.lock` is intentionally stale — `pip install .` is the supported path (same as CI, see `.github/workflows/test.yml`). Installing registers the `spawner` entry point (in `venv/bin/`, so it is only on `PATH` when the venv is activated). `venv/bin/spawner` or `venv/bin/python -m kestrel_team.cli.app` work without activation and are equivalent everywhere below.

## Quickstart

1. Copy `.env.example` to `.env` (loaded from the repo root) and set the key(s) your tier policy needs — the policy lives in `kestrel_team/configs/inference.yaml` (as shipped: a free `GEMINI_API_KEY` from Google AI Studio for the governor tier — no billing account needed — and an OpenAI-compatible endpoint for the utility tier; the frontier tier runs on a logged-in `claude` CLI).

2. Preflight — see resolved routing per persona and what's missing:

   ```bash
   spawner doctor                      # list teams/tiers + environment checks
   spawner doctor --team claude_squad  # per-persona credential preflight (exits nonzero if missing)
   ```

3. Optional, for sandboxed runs and the claude_code executor:

   ```bash
   docker build -f Dockerfile.sandbox -t kestrel-sandbox:latest .
   ```

4. First run:

   ```bash
   spawner spawn -t claude_squad \
     -g "Add a --verbose flag to the CLI and document it" \
     -r /path/to/target/repo --limit 15 --max-budget 2
   ```

   Spawn is fail-closed: it refuses to start (exit 1) if any persona's route is unresolved
   or a required credential is missing — fix the declaration or the key and re-run. The run
   pauses at a human-in-the-loop breakpoint before creating the PR. Structured task files (`--task-file`) are documented in `examples/tasks/README.md`.

5. See what it cost and how it ended:

   ```bash
   spawner runs
   ```

Buying a new inference vendor is paste-a-key, not a code change. The common purchasable providers (`deepseek`, `dashscope` for Alibaba Qwen, `zai` for Zhipu GLM, `moonshot` for Kimi, `mistral`, `xai`, `groq`, `together_ai`, `fireworks_ai`, `openrouter`) are pre-wired in the closed provider registry (`kestrel_team/core/routing.py`, `PROVIDERS`): (1) point a tier in `kestrel_team/configs/inference.yaml` (or a persona) at `provider: <name>` / `model: <model>`; (2) put the key in `.env` (env var names are listed in `.env.example`); (3) run `spawner doctor --team <team>` and confirm the credential shows ✓. See [`docs/drain.md`](docs/drain.md). |

- `OVERVIEW.md` — architecture: control plane, manifests, tiers, executors, governance.
- `docs/run-lifecycle.md` — what actually happens on `spawner spawn`, end to end.
- `docs/capabilities.md` — capability + delegation brief (for another repo/context that delegates to Kestrel).
- `docs/ecosystem-and-strategy.md` — the whole-system read-out + strategy brief (planes, tools, focus, bets).
- `ROADMAP.md` — backlog, single source of truth, plus the task-status protocol.
- `.agent-context/task_lifecycle.md` — the protocol agents follow when working this repo.
- `docs/poc/` — design lessons from the proof-of-concept runs.
- `examples/tasks/` — sample structured task files and their schema.

```bash
venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/ -q

lines: 3.2.1 The Drain (dispatcher lane, ADR-0010)

`spawner drain` is the thin deterministic drain of *shaped* delegation requests. The queue lives in the intent plane (kestrel-helm) as markdown items carrying intake-shaping frontmatter (size class, risk grade, failure policy, mode, optional group); this repo reads them verbatim from `--queue <dir>` / `KESTREL_QUEUE_DIR` and shells `spawner spawn` per selected item. Loosely coupled by design — files + CLI + ledger, no shared imports (see docs/drain.md, docs/queue_item_contract.md).

-Selector-driven, never whole-queue by default: by item id, `--group`, composable `--risk`/`--target`/`--limit`. `--list` previews and exits; a bare `spawner drain` previews the drainable items and asks for a selector; a selected drain previews then requires interactive confirmation before any spawn. Only `mode: delegated` + `status: queued` items are drainable; malformed frontmatter or a missing queue dir is a fail-closed typed error, never a skip.

+Selector-driven, never whole-queue by default: by item id, `--group`, composable `--risk`/`--target`/`--limit`. `--list` previews and exits; a bare `spawner drain` previews the drainable items and asks for a selector; a selected drain previews then requires confirmation before any spawn — interactive on a terminal, or the explicit `--yes` flag, which auto-confirms the preview gate and every forwarded run HITL and announces each one (attended-by-authorization, ADR-0009 rung 2; a prompting drain off a terminal without `--yes` is refused at startup). Only `mode: delegated` + `status: queued` items are drainable; malformed frontmatter or a missing queue dir is a fail-closed typed error, never a skip.

Execution is sequential (MVP): mark the item `running`, spawn as a subprocess (stdin inherited so the run's HITL breakpoint reaches the operator), match the ledger row by thread id, write back `delivered`/`failed`, then apply the item's pre-decided failure policy (`low` continue / `medium` halt the failed item's group / `high` halt the batch). The drain makes no LLM calls and adds no retries beyond a single spawn's.
